verdict.rationale: Basecamp documents a first-party access control: Client mode lets you choose, project by project, what clients can and cannot see. That gives a product manager some visibility control, but the evidence shows no granular role model and no edit-level permissions. missing for 10: defined roles (e.g., admin/owner/member), granular edit vs. view permissions, per-item or per-tool access controls, permission controls for non-client co-workers, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a product manager, I can assign granular permissions and roles to control who can view or edit work

citations.quote: Basecamp’s Client mode lets you decide what they should — and shouldn’t — see, project by project.
